{{Elections in Nebraska}}

The '''2026 United States Senate election in Nebraska''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Nebraska]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Pete Ricketts]] is seeking his first full term following a [[2024 United States Senate special election in Nebraska|special election]] in 2024. Former union leader [[Dan Osborn]], who ran in the [[2024 United States Senate election in Nebraska|2024 regular election]], is again running as an [[Political independent|independent]].

[[Primary elections]] were held on May 12, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2026 Election Calendar|url=https://sos.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/elections/2026/2026_Election_Calendar.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260505151000/https://sos.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/elections/2026/2026_Election_Calendar.pdf|archive-date=May 5, 2026|url-status=live|publisher=[[Secretary of State of Nebraska]]}}</ref> Ricketts won the Republican nomination with 81.5% of the vote. Although [[Nebraska Democratic Party|state Democrats]] endorsed Osborn, pastor William Forbes entered the Democratic primary amid accusations of being a [[Spoiler effect|spoiler candidate]]. In response, retired pharmacy technician Cindy Burbank launched a primary candidacy supported by the party and defeated Forbes with 89.2% of the vote before dropping out of the general election in July to support Osborn.

Republicans have not lost a Senate election in Nebraska since Ricketts lost as its nominee [[2006 United States Senate election in Nebraska|in 2006]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nebraskapublicmedia.org/es/news/news-articles/senate-candidate-dan-osborn-hits-campaign-trail-with-populist-blue-collar-message/|title=Senate candidate Dan Osborn hits campaign trail with populist, blue-collar message|first1=Brian|last1=Beach|publisher=Nebraska Public Media|date=September 23, 2025|access-date=August 14, 2026|quote=Osborn may have lost to Fischer by more than 6 percentage points, but in a state that hasn't elected a non-Republican to the Senate since 2006, the close margin elevated his profile and motivated supporters heading into the next election cycle.}}</ref> The last independent to win a Senate election in Nebraska was progressive [[George W. Norris|George Norris]] in [[1936 United States Senate election in Nebraska|1936]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sainato |first=Michael |date=April 29, 2024 |title=He led a strike at Kellogg's. Now he's aiming for a Nebraska Senate seat |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/apr/29/dan-osborn-nebraska-senate-elections |access-date=May 19, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> This election will be the first in which a state did not have a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidate in back-to-back US Senate election cycles.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://smartpolitics.lib.umn.edu/2025/07/11/will-nebraska-democrats-make-history-in-2026/|title=Will Nebraska Democrats Make History in 2026?|publisher=Smart Politics|date=July 11, 2025|access-date=August 5, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://smartpolitics.lib.umn.edu/2026/08/05/a-brief-history-of-us-senate-elections-without-democrats-on-the-ballot/|title=A Brief History of US Senate Elections without Democrats on the Ballot|publisher=Smart Politics|date=August 5, 2026|access-date=August 5, 2026}}</ref>

== Independent ==
In the [[2024 United States Senate election in Nebraska]], union president [[Dan Osborn]] ran as an [[Independent politician|independent]] against Republican incumbent [[Deb Fischer]], losing by fewer than seven points in one of Nebraska's closest Senate races. Osborn significantly outperformed Democratic nominee [[Preston Love Jr.]], who lost the [[2024 United States Senate special election in Nebraska|concurrent special Senate election]] to Pete Ricketts by more than 24 points.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nebraska U.S. Senate Election Results 2024: Deb Fischer Wins |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/11/05/us/elections/results-nebraska-us-senate.html |access-date=November 7, 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=November 5, 2024}}</ref>

In early 2025, Osborn formed an exploratory committee for a potential 2026 run.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/04/03/dan-osborn-nebraska-senate-00268026|title=Dan Osborn makes moves toward another Nebraska Senate run|date=April 3, 2025|website=[[Politico]]}}</ref> In June 2026, he submitted a petition to appear on the general election ballot as an independent,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dan Osborn submits signatures to challenge Ricketts on Nebraska's November ballot |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/briefs/dan-osborn-submits-signatures-to-challenge-ricketts-on-nebraskas-november-ballot/ |last=Salinas |first=Juan II |work=[[Nebraska Examiner]] |language=en-US |date=June 11, 2026 |access-date=August 7, 2026}}</ref> which was verified the following month.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Nebraska nonpartisan US Senate candidate Dan Osborn qualifies for November ballot |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/07/16/nebraska-nonpartisan-us-senate-candidate-dan-osborn-qualifies-for-november-ballot/ |last=Salinas |first=Juan II |work=[[Nebraska Examiner]] |language=en-US |date=July 16, 2026 |access-date=August 7, 2026}}</ref>

Although Osborn is not affiliated with the [[Nebraska Democratic Party]], the party is supporting his candidacy, citing their greater alignment with his platform.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Cottle|first=Michelle|title=He's Not a Democrat. Democrats Love Him Anyway.|publisher=The New York Times|date=August 11, 2026|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/11/opinion/dan-osborn-nebraska-independent-democrats.html|access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

== Democratic primary ==
=== Background ===
[[Jane Kleeb]], the chair of the [[Nebraska Democratic Party]], said the party did not intend to recruit a candidate, similar to the [[2024 United States Senate election in Nebraska#Democratic primary|Nebraska Senate race]] in 2024.<ref name="Downballot">{{cite web|last1=Nir|first1=David|last2=Singer|first2=Jeff|title=Morning Digest: Nebraska independent who spooked GOP launches another Senate bid|url=https://www.the-downballot.com/p/morning-digest-nebraska-independent|website=The Downballot|access-date=July 10, 2025|date=July 9, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/12/us/politics/nebraska-election-takeaways-dan-osborn-ricketts-senate.html |title=Democrat Wins Senate Primary in Nebraska, but Plans to Drop Out |last=Browning |first=Kellen |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=May 12, 2026 |access-date=May 17, 2026}}</ref> In August 2025, the party endorsed [[Dan Osborn]], an independent candidate.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Coblerobler|first=Ariana Joy|date=August 1, 2025|title=Dan Osborn endorsed by NE Democratic Party for 2026 Senate race|url=https://nebraska.tv/news/local/dan-osborn-endorsed-by-ne-democratic-party-for-2026-senate-race|access-date=November 16, 2025|publisher=NTV}}</ref> 

In March 2026, the party called for Democratic candidate William Forbes to withdraw, with Kleeb accusing him of trying to "trick voters" and opposing abortion access. She urged Democrats to support Osborn instead.<ref name="Slew" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kleeb |first=Jane |author-link=Jane Kleeb |date=March 3, 2026 |title=NDP Press Release - Statement on U.S. Senate Candidate William Forbes |url=https://nebraskademocrats.org/blog/ndp-press-release-statement-on-u-s-senate-candidate-william-forbes/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260318172758/https://nebraskademocrats.org/blog/ndp-press-release-statement-on-u-s-senate-candidate-william-forbes/ |archive-date=March 18, 2026 |access-date=March 18, 2026 |publisher=[[Nebraska Democratic Party]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In an interview with [[CNN]], Forbes acknowledged that he had voted for Donald Trump in multiple elections, but insisted that he was a lifelong Democrat.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaczynski |first=Andrew |author-link=Andrew Kaczynski |date=March 30, 2026 |title=The Trump-voting pastor Democrats think could cost them a chance at a Nebraska Senate seat |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/03/30/politics/nebraska-senate-trump-pastor |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260330133625/https://edition.cnn.com/2026/03/30/politics/nebraska-senate-trump-pastor |archive-date=March 30, 2026 |access-date=May 20, 2026 |publisher=[[CNN]] |language=en |quote=In an interview with CNN, Forbes said he's voted for President Donald Trump in multiple elections but denied being a Republican plant, insisting that he's a lifelong Democrat. Asked repeatedly to name a Democrat he voted for, Forbes grew frustrated and said the party needed to return to the "morality" it represented under President John F. Kennedy.}}</ref> 

After Forbes entered the race retired pharmacy technician Cindy Burbank launched a primary candidacy endorsed by the state party. On March 17, 2026, [[Secretary of State of Nebraska]] [[Bob Evnen]] removed Burbank from the ballot following a complaint from [[Nebraska Republican Party]] that alleged she was not a good-faith candidate.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salinas II |first=Juan |date=March 17, 2026 |title=Evnen removes Nebraska Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Burbank from ballot |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/03/17/evnen-removes-nebraska-democratic-u-s-senate-candidate-burbank-from-ballot/ |access-date=March 23, 2026 |website=[[Nebraska Examiner]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Burbank filed a lawsuit in [[Lancaster County, Nebraska|Lancaster County]] District Court immediately following the removal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nebraska Democratic Senate candidate Burbank sues to get back on the ballot |url=https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/nebraska-democratic-senate-candidate-burbank-sues-get-back-ballot |access-date=March 23, 2026 |website=[[News From The States]] |language=en}}</ref> On March 19, 2026, a District Court judge dismissed Burbank's lawsuit.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salinas II |first=Juan |date=March 19, 2026 |title=Nebraska Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Burbank stays off ballot after lawsuit dismissal — for now |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/03/19/nebraska-democratic-u-s-senate-candidate-burbank-stays-off-ballot-after-case-dismissal-for-now/ |access-date=March 23, 2026 |website=[[Nebraska Examiner]] |language=en-US}}</ref> On March 23, 2026, the [[Nebraska Supreme Court]] ruled that Evnen missed a deadline to consider complaints and reinstated Burbank to the ballot.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salinas II |first=Juan |date=March 23, 2026 |title=Court orders Nebraska candidate back on U.S. Senate ballot, says Evnen acted late |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/03/23/nebraska-u-s-senate-candidate-back-on-ballot-state-high-court-rules-sos-acted-too-late/ |access-date=March 23, 2026 |website=[[Nebraska Examiner]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Burbank stated in April that she would consider leaving the race to "unify the votes" against Ricketts.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.ketv.com/article/nebraskas-primary-democratic-candidates-us-senate/71154257 |title=2 Democratic candidates run for US Senate in Nebraska's primary |last=Carlson |first=Beth |publisher=[[KETV]] |date=April 28, 2026|access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref> She said in a phone interview a week before the primary that she intended to withdraw from the general election and would support Osborn if there was "no clear path to victory".<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/democrats-nebraska-senate-primary-dan-osborn-pete-ricketts-rcna344474|title=Democrats pick Nebraska Senate nominee who could drop out and back independent Dan Osborn|date=May 13, 2026|publisher=NBC News|last=Bowman |first=Bridget |access-date=July 23, 2026 |language=en}}</ref> She filed to be removed from the ballot on July 17,<ref name="BurbankWithdrawal">{{Cite news |url=https://www.ketv.com/article/nebraska-senate-democrat-candidate-cindy-burbank-ballot-removal/73172106 |title=Cindy Burbank, Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Nebraska, asks to be removed from ballot |last=Anderson |first=Jake |work=[[KETV]] |date=July 17, 2026 |access-date=July 17, 2026}}</ref> which was confirmed by Secretary of State Evnen on July 21.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.1011now.com/2026/07/21/nebraska-democrats-must-find-new-senate-candidate-after-burbank-declines-nomination/|title=Nebraska Democrats must find a new Senate candidate after Burbank declines nomination |first=Abigail |last=Carrera|date=July 21, 2026 |website=[[1011now]]}}</ref>

After Burbank's withdrawal, Forbes filed a lawsuit which claimed the Nebraska Democratic Party must have a Senate candidate.<ref>{{Cite website |last=Ashford |first=Molly |title=Arguing that Nebraska Democrats must have a Senate candidate, primary loser says he's willing |publisher=Nebraska Public Media |date=August 3, 2026 |url=https://nebraskapublicmedia.org/en/news/news-articles/arguing-that-nebraska-democrats-must-have-a-senate-candidate-primary-loser-says-hes-willing/}}</ref> An initial ruling by a Lancaster County judge stated that the attempt to force the party to field a candidate was unlikely to succeed and raised "serious constitutional concerns."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ashford |first=Molly |date=August 7, 2026 |title=Judge says effort to force Nebraska Dems to replace vacancy on ballot unlikely to succeed |url=https://nebraskapublicmedia.org/en/news/news-articles/judge-says-effort-to-force-nebraska-dems-to-replace-vacancy-on-ballot-unlikely-to-succeed/ |url-status=live |access-date=August 9, 2026 |publisher=[[Nebraska Public Media]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The case was dismissed on August 26, 2026.<ref>https://www.courthousenews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/forbes-v-nebraska-democratic-party-defendant-order-summary-judgment.pdf</ref>

== Third parties==
=== America First Party ===
[[America First Party (2026)|America First Party]] organizers submitted completed petitions to form a new party on July 15, 2026; registered voter signatures required to do so were verified by the Nebraska Secretary of State on August 7, 2026.<ref name="auto1">{{cite press release |last=State of Nebraska Secretary of State |title=Nebraska Working People Party and America First Party meet signature threshold for political party formation |publisher=State of Nebraska |date=August 7, 2026 |url=https://sos.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/news-releases/Nebraska%20Working%20People%20Party%20and%20America%20First%20Party%20meet%20signature%20threshold%20for%20political%20party%20formation.pdf |access-date=September 3, 2026}}</ref> After a ruling by the [[Nebraska Supreme Court]] on August 26, 2026, against the [[Nebraska Republican Party]] objections (which claimed the party's name would cause confusion for voters) the secretary confirmed the party's formation.<ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Salinas II |first=Juan |title=Nebraska Supreme Court clears the way for two new Nebraska political parties|newspaper=The Nebraska Examiner |date=August 26, 2026 |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/08/26/nebraska-supreme-court-clears-the-way-for-two-new-nebraska-political-parties/|access-date=September 4, 2026}}</ref> Chuck Conboy, an account manager, is the party's nominee in this race.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Newly formed America First Party announces five candidates for Nebraska elections |url=https://nebraskapublicmedia.org/en/news/news-articles/newly-formed-america-first-party-announces-five-candidates-for-nebraska-elections/ |last=Olberding |first=Matt |work=[[Nebraska Public Media]] |language=en |date=September 1, 2026 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

===Legal Marijuana NOW primary===
Prior to the primary, Mark Elworth Jr., the former chair of the [[Nebraska Legal Marijuana Now|Legal Marijuana NOW]] party, accused Mike Marvin of being a "Dan Osborn plant".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Salinas |first1=Julia |title=Nebraska U.S. Senate race filled with alleged 'plants', campaigns say |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/03/03/nebraska-u-s-senate-race-filled-with-alleged-plants-campaigns-say/ |website=[[Nebraska Examiner]] |access-date=May 18, 2026|date=March 3, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260512232406/https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/03/03/nebraska-u-s-senate-race-filled-with-alleged-plants-campaigns-say/|archive-date=May 12, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> In addition, Republicans accused Marvin of planning to drop out and endorse Osborn if he won the nomination. Marvin has denied the allegations.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bailey |first1=Philip |title=Nebraska Senate race hinges on accusations of trying to 'trick' voters |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/05/12/nebraska-senate-ricketts-osborn-trick-voters/90028238007/ |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=May 18, 2026|date=May 12, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260512105530/https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/05/12/nebraska-senate-ricketts-osborn-trick-voters/90028238007/|archive-date=May 12, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Cindy Burbank, the Democratic nominee, paid for Marvin's $1,740 filing fee when the [[Secretary of State of Nebraska|secretary of state]] refused to take his own check, which had the incorrect amount.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salinas II |first=Juan |date=March 24, 2026 |title=Nebraska Dem Senate candidate Burbank paid third-party candidate's filing fee |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/03/24/nebraska-dem-senate-candidate-burbank-paid-third-party-candidates-filing-fee/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507235141/https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/03/24/nebraska-dem-senate-candidate-burbank-paid-third-party-candidates-filing-fee/ |archive-date=May 7, 2026 |access-date=May 20, 2026 |website=[[Nebraska Examiner]] |language=en-US |quote=Burbank, in a follow-up email Tuesday, told the Examiner she was in the election office in early March and saw 'the secretary's people refusing to take Mike's check because it was for ten dollars too much.' ... 'It pissed me off, and I paid for it ... I've never met Mike,' Burbank said. 'If Ricketts can throw his money around then so can I!'}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Browning |first=Kellen |date=May 11, 2026 |title=G.O.P. Plant? Democratic Ruse? Accusations Fly in Nebraska's Senate Race |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/11/us/politics/nebraska-senate-race-primary.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=May 20, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |quote=Ms. Burbank said there was no collusion, and that she encountered Mr. Marvin at the secretary of state's office when both were submitting candidate applications. There was an issue with Mr. Marvin's filing check, Ms. Burbank said, so she paid for him.}}</ref> Marvin did not submit the paperwork to be removed from the ballot before the August 3 deadline,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Salinas |first1=Juan |title=Legal Marijuana NOW candidate will stay on fall ballot for Nebraska US Senate |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/briefs/legal-marijuana-now-candidate-will-stay-on-fall-ballot-for-nebraska-us-senate/ |website=[[Nebraska Examiner]] |access-date=August 4, 2026}}</ref> but withdrew and endorsed Osborn on August 21, citing a health condition. He will remain on the ballot.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Annonen |first=Noelle |title=Legal Marijuana NOW candidate drops out of Nebraska Senate race |url=https://nebraskapublicmedia.org/en/news/news-articles/legal-marijuana-now-candidate-drops-out-of-nebraska-senate-race/ |access-date=October 2, 2026 |website=Nebraska Public Media|date=August 21, 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Nebraska Working People Party ===
Nebraska Working People Party organizers submitted completed petitions to form a new party on July 14 and was verified by the Secretary of State on August 7, 2026.<ref name="auto1"/> After a ruling by the [[Nebraska Supreme Court]] on August 26, 2026, that the [[Nebraska Democratic Party]]'s objection (claiming that the name is too similar to the [[Working Families Party]]) had been filed too late, the secretary confirmed the party's formation.<ref name="auto2"/> Robin Richards, the party's chair, is the party's nominee in this race.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2026|title=Nebraska Working People Party Chair Richards running for U.S. Senate herself |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/briefs/nebraska-working-people-party-chair-richards-running-for-u-s-senate-herself/ |access-date=September 3, 2026 |website=[[Nebraska Examiner]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
